shareErrors.notAShareFile: That file is not a Diff Bro shared diff.
shareErrors.notForYou: This shared diff is sealed for a different machine — it can only be opened by its addressed recipient.
shareErrors.tampered: Rejected: the file was modified in transit (or is corrupted) — decryption failed.
shareErrors.unknownSigner: Sealed correctly, but signed by an unknown sender — add their public key first (File → Add Trusted Key).
shareErrors.badSignature: Signature check failed — the file was modified or corrupted.
shareErrors.badTrustedKey: The stored public key for this sender is unreadable — remove it and add their key file again.
shareErrors.expired: This shared diff has already expired.
shareErrors.invalidTtl: Rejected: shared diffs cannot live longer than a week.
shareErrors.unknownRecipient: Recipient not found among trusted keys.
shareErrors.renamed: This shared diff was renamed — its integrity is tied to its original hashed filename, so it was refused. Ask the sender to re-send it unchanged.
shareErrors.identityUnavailable: Your identity key couldn’t be unlocked (the OS keychain may be locked). Nothing was changed — unlock it and try again.
shareErrors.vaultKeyUnavailable: The saved-diff key couldn’t be unlocked (the OS keychain may be locked). Your saved diffs and snippets are intact — unlock it and try again.
shareErrors.notASnippetFile: That file is not a Diff Bro snippets export.
shareErrors.wrongPassphrase: Wrong passphrase, or the file is corrupted.
shareErrors.corrupted: The file could not be read after decryption.
shareErrors.malformed: That snippets file is not shaped like a valid export and was rejected.
shareErrors.tooLarge: That snippets file exceeds the allowed size limits and was rejected.

compare.title: Two files, any way you like
compare.body: Drop them anywhere on this window, or click a slot to browse. Diff Bro picks the viewer for you — text, JSON tree, spreadsheet grid or diagram.

share.title: Send it sealed, not screenshotted
share.body: Share locks this comparison so only the people you pick can open it, and it stops opening after however long you choose. First time with someone, you swap a small key file: Security ▸ Share My Public Key sends yours, Security ▸ Add Trusted Key takes theirs. After that it is two clicks.

library.title: Your library, narrowing as you type
library.body: Saved diffs, shared diffs and snippets all live here. Watch the list filter as the search fills in.

quick-look.title: The same search, over any app
quick-look.body: Press {shortcut} and this box opens on top of whatever you are working in — even while Diff Bro is minimised. Find a snippet, copy it, press Escape. Try it now.

settings-open.title: The rest is in the menus
settings-open.body: Fourteen themes, size limits, where your data is kept, the shortcut above — all of it is in Settings, at the bottom of the File menu.

settings-panes.title: One pane at a time
settings-panes.body: Everything else is down this list — Shortcuts for the quick look-up chord, Storage for where your data is kept, Limits for how large a file may be.

settings-tips.title: And this is the off switch
settings-tips.body: Tips appear again after an update. Turn them off here — or press Show tour whenever you want this walk-through back.

snippet-new.title: Save commonly used text or code
snippet-new.body: A deploy payload, a prompt, a config block — the + here starts one, and the search finds it again next week.

snippet-save.title: Name it, tag it, save it
snippet-save.body: This one is filled in already. Press the ringed Save to keep it — the sidebar and the quick look-up both find it afterwards. Next moves on either way.

snippet-drag.title: Drag it anywhere in here
snippet-drag.body: The whole comparison area takes a drop — you don’t have to land on a file box. A snippet can face a file, or another snippet.

diagram-open.title: A Mermaid snippet draws itself
diagram-open.body: This one is a diagram — it previews live as you type it. Two versions of one compare as a picture rather than as text.

diagram.title: A diagram change, as a diagram
diagram.body: Here it is: the same flow, one revision apart. Every added, removed or changed node is marked on the picture, so you read the change instead of hunting for it in the text.
